title: The Concert Hall Where Rain Takes Requests

features.name: sound chamber
features.desc-on-touch: A speaker cone renders in pale wireframe—you hear the rain playing through it before you hear the speaker itself.

features.name: request desk
features.desc-on-touch: The ledger open before you lists each storm by the emotional frequency it broadcast on—each line a conversation between weather and witness.

features.name: listening stations
features.desc-on-touch: Twin amphitheater seats with no floor—you sit in sound itself, held by nothing but the rain's attention.

features.name: entry arch
features.desc-on-touch: The threshold hums—rain entering becomes music; music exiting becomes rain again.

features.name: wet microphone
features.desc-on-touch: Beaded with water that doesn't fall—each droplet catches a frequency, a small translation between weather and voice.

reverie.title: REVERIE — concert hall where rain learns to want listeners
narr: You both sit in the amphitheater seat, listening to the rain
as if it had traveled through every speaker in the archive to
reach you both at once. Her shoulder touches yours. The rain
outside sounds nothing like the rain played through the hall's
speakers—but for a moment, they sync. You hear her hear it.
Then the room releases you back into separate rain.

inscription: here the rain learns it was always music, and the music learns it was always weather

file.name: ConcertArchive_RainfallRecitals_Request_Log_1989-2001.txt
file.note: Ledger of every storm that came through with a song; each entry describes the frequency at which that rain learned to become music.
